svg.title: Delta write optimization decision
svg.desc: Delta write optimization decision. Observe the table symptom; Read layout is inefficient?; Too many small output files?; Update-heavy workload?; Existing files fragmented?; Check engine compatibility; Measure and maintain.
svg.text: Delta Write Optimization — Which Technique, and What It Costs

g.title: Measure and maintain — Validate scan cost, write duration, file count, and correctness after the change.
g.text: Four techniques operate at different points in the write/read lifecycle. Each buys read or write efficiency at a measured price.

svg.text: DECISION SPINE — WHAT PROBLEM AM I SOLVING?

g.title: Observe the table symptom — File count, scan behavior, update pattern, and consumer engines identify the real Delta problem.
g.text: "Reads are slow" → V-Order "Writes scatter tiny files" → Optimized Write "Row-level UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE is expensive" → Deletion Vectors "Small files already piled up" → Compaction

g.title: Read layout is inefficient? — V-Order optimizes Parquet organization for analytical reads in Fabric.
g.text: These are not mutually exclusive — a mutation-heavy production table typically runs Optimized Write + Auto Compaction always on, and evaluates V-Order and deletion vectors against its own workload shape.

svg.text: Techniques compose: V-Order is file-level and stacks with Z-Order, compaction, vacuum, and time travel.

g.text: 1 · V-Order
write-time Parquet reshape
Reorders row groups, encoding, and compression at
write time — logical data is unchanged, so query
results are identical. Files stay fully spec-compliant
Parquet; only Fabric engines get the read speed-up.
BENEFIT
Reads improve significantly — best for
COST
~15% slower writes
(Microsoft's stated average)
Use when:
dashboarding, interactive analytics, repeated scans, Direct Lake tables
Skip when:
write-dominated ingestion/transform pipelines — pays the tax with no reader
Off by default in new workspaces. Controlled at session, table-property, or
per-write level — session/write settings override the table property.
Direct Lake bonus: better RLE compression speeds transcoding into VertiPaq,
2 · Optimized Write
shuffle before write
Shuffles data across executors before writing so each
partition is handled by one executor, producing fewer,
larger files. Target size set by BinSize (default 1 GB;
256 MB general workloads, 128 MB small workloads).
BENCHMARK — WIN
1,823 partitions: 6:43 → 53s write,
175,008 → 1,823 files, 19x faster queries
BENCHMARK — LOSS
non-partitioned: 35% slower
writes, 2x slower queries
Use when:
many partitions, streaming micro-batches feeding the table
Skip when:
non-partitioned table where fewer files hurt read parallelism
Fragmentation without it costs compression too: ~33% more data
on disk in a partitioned benchmark when disabled.
UPDATE/MERGE + deletion vectors still fragment files even with this on.
3 · Deletion Vectors
copy-on-write → merge-on-read
Instead of rewriting a whole Parquet file for a changed
record, affected row positions go into a small .bin file
referenced from the add action; rows are filtered out
at query time instead of being physically removed.
BENEFIT (100M-row benchmark)
single-row delete ~8x faster,
33% mass delete ~2.5x faster,
READ-TIME MERGE COST
2.3x slower reads if unmaintained
(53% non-append changes, no compaction)
Use when:
write-heavy pipelines that pair it with a real OPTIMIZE/VACUUM cadence
Skip when:
no maintenance cadence exists, or readers can't handle protocol 2.3+
Enabling permanently raises minReaderVersion to 3 / minWriterVersion to 7.
After OPTIMIZE, read performance matches copy-on-write exactly.
Caveat: Polars/delta-rs raises DeltaProtocolError; Fabric Copy Activity unsupported.
4 · Compaction — OPTIMIZE / Auto Compaction
Auto Compaction fires after writes once small-file
count in a partition passes minNumFiles (default 50),
merging files under minFileSize toward maxFileSize
(default 128 MB). Manual OPTIMIZE runs on demand.
BEST COMBO (200-iter benchmark)

g.title: Update-heavy workload? — Deletion vectors record row deletions without immediately rewriting every affected data file.
g.text: Auto Compaction + Optimized Write:
12.77 min total, file-count stdev 14
WORST — NO COMPACTION
33.27 min total runtime
file-count stdev 864
Use when:
always-on for tables <1 GB; add scheduled OPTIMIZE above 1 GB
Watch for:
a past Fabric runtime bug over-triggered on tables >1 GB (now fixed)
Optimized Write alone cut per-iteration files ~16→1, but periodic
compaction is still needed to consolidate into the 500 MB–1 GB range.
Auto-triggered runs are tagged operationParameters.auto=true in the log.

svg.text: Measured benefit — from the cited benchmark or vendor-stated figure

g.title: Check engine compatibility — Every table feature must be supported by all required writers and readers.
g.text: Measured cost / trade-off — the price paid for that benefit

svg.text: All benchmark figures are from the cited authors' own controlled test environments and are directional, not universal guarantees — treat them as
evidence of the trade-off's shape, not a promise of identical numbers on your workload.

g.title: Too many small output files? — Optimized Write reshapes Spark output to produce more appropriately sized files.
